Now I see the pattern more clearly:
When I clicked the blue block (upper one at rows 24-27):
- Upper white region: bbox changed from [1,32]-[27,63] to [1,28]-[27,63] - expanded LEFT by 4 columns (from col 32 to col 28), pixels went from 848 to 956 (+108)
- Lower white region: bbox changed from [32,52]-[63,63] to [32,56]-[63,63] - shrunk LEFT by 4 columns (from col 52 to col 56), pixels went from 368 to 240 (-128)
- Gray region: expanded RIGHT from col 51 to col 55 (+20 pixels)
So clicking the upper blue block:
1. Expanded the upper white region to the left (4 columns)
2. Shrunk the lower white region from the left (4 columns)
3. Expanded the gray region to the right (4 columns)
This is interesting - it seems like clicking a blue block causes a "shift" in the boundary between gray and white regions. The blue block acts as a control point.
Let me think about this differently. The gray region seems to be "consuming" the white regions. The blue blocks are like levers that shift the boundary. The goal might be to eliminate all white regions (or all gray regions) by clicking the right blue blocks.
Let me try clicking the lower blue block to see what it does.
